what: Test of No Group Discrimination Using the WMW Statistic
title: Test of No Group Discrimination Using the WMW Statistic
text: classical Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney (WMW) test calibrated null hypothesis H0:F=G\mathrm{H_0\colon F = G}. However, WMW test statistic, standardized, empirical AUC (eAUC), hence test fact assesses set {(F,G):AUC=0.5}\lbrace\mathrm{(F,G)\colon AUC = 0.5}\rbrace, match H0:F=G\mathrm{H_0\colon F = G}. incoherence (Grendár 2026) causes WMW test provides erroneous inferences. wmwAUC implements properly calibrated test H0:AUC=0.5\mathrm{H_0\colon AUC = 0.5} based WMW statistic; details, see (Grendár 2025). package provides asymptotic inference two finite-sample bias-correction methods: Exact Unbiased (EU) Method: Universal approach handling data arbitrary tie patterns mid-rank kernel exact finite-sample unbiased variance estimation Hoeffding decomposition theory. Reduces correctly continuous case ties present. Bias-Corrected (BC) Method: Alternative method using individual placement-component bias correction O(n−1)O(n^{-1}) finite-sample corrections Welch-Satterthwaite degrees freedom. Derived continuous data (Sect. 4 paper); implementation extends ties via mid-rank kernel EU, conservative behavior confirmed simulation persist ties. EU method serves default implementation, providing: Universal applicability (handles data type - continuous, discrete, mixed) Exact finite-sample unbiasedness (asymptotic approximation) Theoretically principled tie handling mid-rank kernel Retained real power small sample sizes BC’s power can close zero BC remains available users specifically want conservative behavior. Key functions include: wmwAUC_test(): Main testing function, defaulting EU method, option select BC instead wmwAUC_pvalue_BC(): WMW AUC p-values via BC method wmwAUC_pvalue_EU(): WMW AUC p-values via EU method, valid tie pattern wmwAUC_pseudomedian_ci(): Confidence interval AUC-equalizing shift (pseudomedian), obtained inverting test (old names wmw_test(), wmw_pvalue(), wmw_pvalue_ties(), pseudomedian_ci() retained functional aliases. Calling raises informative error naming current function use instead.)

title: Confidence Interval for the AUC-Equalizing Shift (Hodges-Lehmann Pseudomedian) via Test Inversion — wmwAUC_pseudomedian_ci
text: pseudomedian \(\delta\) defined generally, pair distributions \(F, G\), shift solving \(P(X < Y + \delta) = 0.5\) — .e. value \(\delta\) equalizes AUC \(X\) shifted \(Y + \delta\). definition require location-shift model relating \(F\) \(G\). location-shift (\(F(t) = G(t - \Delta)\)), \(\delta\) coincides classical Hodges-Lehmann pseudomedian equals location difference \(\Delta\); special case, definition. Outside location-shift, \(\delta\) remains well-defined AUC-equalizing shift, read "median difference" two groups. confidence interval obtained grid search candidate \(\delta\) values, retaining AUC=0.5 test applied \((X, Y+\delta)\) rejected level 1 - conf.level. search range set heuristically \(\pm 3\) times robust MAD scale pairwise differences around point estimate; true interval extends beyond range, acceptance region contiguous (can occur small, imbalanced samples), warning issued. See Warnings. EU BC pseudomedian CIs computed independent calls, may occasionally reported numerically identical coarse n_grid even though underlying p-value curves genuinely differ — methods' crossing points can land discrete grid cell. small min(length(x), length(y)), BC's near-zero power (see wmwAUC_pvalue_BC) can make pseudomedian interval wide largely uninformative rather merely conservative, since grid search rarely rejects anywhere searched range. EU recommended regime; see warning issued . pvalue_method = 'EU' length(x) + length(y) < 20, grid point's p-value may come Monte Carlo permutation (see wmwAUC_pvalue_EU), making function's result stochastic small sample sizes. reproducible results, call set.seed() immediately beforehand.

title: Confidence Interval for the AUC-Equalizing Shift (Hodges-Lehmann Pseudomedian) via Test Inversion — wmwAUC_pseudomedian_ci

Search range narrow: p-value dropped \(\alpha\) either edge search grid, true endpoint may lie outside searched range; consider widening range increasing n_grid.

title: P-value for the Bias-Corrected (BC) Test of AUC — wmwAUC_pvalue_BC
text: BC estimates \(\mathrm{Var}(\hat )\) correcting placement-variance component \(O(1/n)\) upward bias, using plug-estimate bias subtracted naive placement variance; corrected component floored independently small \(\epsilon > 0\) otherwise go negative. mid-rank kernel \(h(x,y) = 1\{x<y\} + \frac{1}{2} 1\{x=y\}\) used throughout, point estimate variance components. Uses one-tier approach \(\hat\sigma^2_{\mathrm{adj}}\). BC conservative test: observed size stays nominal across wide range sample sizes, heteroskedasticity, tie proportions, real cost power small imbalanced samples. See min_n_warn_threshold warning text; EU method (wmwAUC_pvalue_EU) recommended min(n1, n2) small. x taken represent cases y reference/control group, matching convention wilcox.test(). Internally, test statistic variance components computed \(P(X<Y)\) framework.

title: wmwAUC Test of No Group Discrimination — wmwAUC_test
text: function tests null hypothesis \(\mathrm{H_0\colon AUC} = 0.5\) \(\mathrm{H_1\colon AUC} \neq 0.5\), AUC represents Area ROC Curve. Exact Unbiased ('EU') method used default computing p-values. Bias-Corrected ('BC') method available pvalue_method = 'BC' markedly conservative small imbalanced sample sizes; EU recommended unless BC's specific properties wanted (see wmwAUC_pvalue_BC). Following convention wilcox.test() AUC equals probability \(P(X > Y)\) randomly selected observation first group exceeds randomly selected observation second group. response ~ group, observations non-reference group constitute \(X\), observations reference group (specified ref_level) constitute \(Y\). Thus AUC = P(non-reference > reference). ref_level specified, first factor level used reference. \(U\)-statistic resulting empirical AUC (eAUC) calculated consistently group assignment. test statistic eAUC, estimates true AUC. empirical ROC curve (eROC) constructed varying classification threshold across observed values computing sensitivity 1-specificity threshold. pseudomedian = TRUE, function additionally reports AUC-equalizing shift \(\delta\), defined value solving \(P(X < Y + \delta) = 0.5\); see wmwAUC_pseudomedian_ci details. Confidence intervals true AUC computed using either DeLong et al. (1988) structural-components method based asymptotic normality, bootstrap resampling. bootstrap resampling selected, also used constructing confidence band ROC curve. function can call two independent sources randomness: bootstrap resampling (ci_method = 'boot'), , pseudomedian = TRUE small sample (n1 + n2 < 20), wmwAUC_pvalue_EU's Monte Carlo permutation fallback, called per grid point inside wmwAUC_pseudomedian_ci. reproducible results, call set.seed() immediately wmwAUC_test() rather relying ambient RNG state; single seed covers sources, since draw stream fixed order.

title: wmwAUC 1.0.0
text: Two related corrections BC’s placement-variance components: Denominator fix. var_G_X/var_F_Y (corresponding manuscript quantities zeta1hat^2/zeta2hat^2) now use n1/n2 denominator, n1-1/n2-1. Bessel’s -1 correction justified centering estimated mean; term centers fixed, known value 1-A0/A0, apply. corrected denominator, E[zeta1hat^2] = zeta1^2 + omega1/n2 holds exactly (asymptotic remainder). Higher-order correction removed. (1 - 1/n1 - 1/n2) shrinkage applied top sigma2_adj longer applied. compensating bias denominator fix now removes source; bias gone, applying old shrinkage top overcorrects, underestimating true variance 11-23% (worst small n) rather correcting . sigma2_adj alone now final variance estimator BC uses test statistic; sigma2_final remains.

title: wmwAUC 1.0.0
text: Bug treating one-sided alternative, fixed. wmwAUC_test()’s displayed auc alternative argument use P(case > reference) convention (matching wilcox.test()), wmwAUC_pvalue_EU()/wmwAUC_pvalue_BC() internally test P(X < Y) convention. Calling directly wmwAUC_pvalue_EU(x_vals, y_vals, ...) silently invert meaning alternative = "greater"/"less" relative wmwAUC_test() documents (two-sided p-values unaffected, since test symmetric ). Fixed swapping argument order call site – wmwAUC_pvalue_EU(y_vals, x_vals, alternative = alternative) – rather altering alternative string , internal P(X < Y) becomes P(reference < case) = P(case > reference), matching wmwAUC_test()’s convention exactly. Verified direct construction case cases stochastically larger reference: fix, alternative = "greater" correctly gives small p-value "less" large one; without , come backwards. wmwAUC_pseudomedian_ci() affected – alternative argument always tests two-sided internally.
